name: John Law
seat: Congress member
note: Received the award for attending the most Congress meetings on 7 October 2003. He questioned or spoke in debate at almost every meeting of the year, moved the amendments to the plus/minus grading resolution on 14 October 2003, and moved to table the January-term resolution on 2 March 2004.

name: Robert Watkins
seat: Congress member; chair, Legislative Research Committee; elected Speaker of the Senate 13 April 2004
note: Won $50 Big Red Dollars in the Congress attendance promotion on 30 March 2004, moved to suspend the bylaws on 14 October 2003, wrote the new Constitution and Bylaws, and was nominated Outstanding Congress Member on 6 April 2004. He chaired Legislative Research from at least 28 October 2003, but the Congress attendance award and the Outstanding Congress Member nomination name him as a Congress member in his own right.

name: Katie Dawson
seat: Congress member; co-chair, Student Affairs Committee
note: Won $50 Big Red Dollars for Congress attendance on 20 April 2004 and moved to suspend the bylaws on 2 March 2004 to seat Dana Lockhart on the Judicial Council. She was sworn in on 2 September 2003 as a committee head, a separate class from Congress members, but the Congress attendance award names her as a Congress member.

name: Katie Petit
seat: Congress member
note: Moved an amendment to Bill 03-04-F on the chamber sign letters on 7 October 2003, and answered a question about the size of the proposed broadband fee on 27 January 2004. Name printed three times as "Penit" and once as "Petit"; see spelling doubts.

name: Cameron Yancey
seat: Congress member; Sergeant at Arms from 16 September 2003
note: Seconded the motion to approve the minutes on 2 September 2003, before his appointment as Sergeant at Arms was approved on 16 September 2003. He also questioned the Greek Village financing on 26 August 2003 and the timing of the January term on 9 March 2004.

name: Brittany Fausey
seat: Congress member; co-chair, Public Relations Committee; Coordinator of Committees from 2 March 2004
note: Moved to approve the minutes on 2 September 2003 and was nominated Congress Member of the Month for January/February 2004. She was sworn in on 2 September 2003 as a committee head, a separate class from Congress members, so she is listed here on the strength of the motion and the Congress-level nomination rather than on the swearing-in.

name: Tim Howard
seat: Congress member; co-chair, Student Affairs Committee
note: Seconded Robert Watkins's motion to suspend the bylaws on 14 October 2003 and spoke in the plus/minus grading debate the same night. He also headed Student Affairs, a separate class from Congress members, so he is listed here on the strength of the seconded motion and his floor speeches.

name: Shawn Peavie
seat: Congress member; chair, Campus Improvements Committee
note: Moved to suspend the bylaws to take up the crosswalks resolution on 20 April 2004, and defended Campus Improvements legislation on the floor through the year. He was sworn in on 2 September 2003 as a committee head, a separate class from Congress members, so he is listed here on the strength of the motion.

name: Evelina Petkova
seat: Congress member; co-chair, Public Relations Committee
note: Named Congress Member of September on 21 October 2003, and defended the promotional items and chamber sign letters bills on the floor on 7 October 2003. She headed Public Relations, a separate class from Congress members, so she is listed here on the strength of the Congress Member of the Month award.

name: Matthew Pava
seat: Congress member; Information Technology Director
note: Named Congress Member of October on 18 November 2003, having been nominated on 4 November, and spoke in the debate on the hooded sweatshirts resolution on 2 December 2003. He reported each week as Information Technology Director, an appointed post.

name: Anna Bisig
seat: Congress member
note: Nominated for Congress Member of the Month for January/February 2004 on 2 March 2004 and again on 9 March, and nominated Outstanding Congress Member on 6 April 2004.

name: Scott Wolfe
seat: Congress member; Coordinator of Committees to March 2004
note: Spoke against the plus/minus grading system in floor debate on 14 October 2003, saying his classes and professors opposed it. He reported weekly as Coordinator of Committees until Brittany Fausey replaced him on 2 March 2004.

name: Willie Cravens
seat: Congress member
note: Questioned how the chamber sign letters would be fixed to the wall on 7 October 2003, argued in the plus/minus grading debate on 14 October 2003 that the case against the change had been overstated, and questioned the proposed broadband fee on 27 January 2004.

name: Robert Reynolds
seat: Congress member
note: Asked in the plus/minus grading debate on 14 October 2003 how seriously the objection would be taken, and asked on 2 December 2003 whether the new constitution's discriminatory clause could be made more specific. A different person from Katie Reynolds.

name: Natalina Elliot
seat: Congress member
note: Explained in debate on 14 October 2003 why no bench was put under the proposed shuttle shelter, and reported the same night that students she had spoken to after the forum were indifferent or against plus/minus grading.

name: Michael Kaelin
seat: Congress member
note: Asked during John Law's technology report on 27 January 2004 what kind of line would be used if the residence-hall internet connection were upgraded.

name: Michael Holcomb
seat: Congress member
note: Proposed a compromise in the debate on the hooded sweatshirts resolution on 2 December 2003, that some go to Congress members and some to the student body. He was also named in the perfect attendance awards of 14 October 2003.

name: Mary Johns
seat: Congress member
note: Asked repeatedly from the floor: whom plus/minus grading would really affect on 23 September 2003, who would check the online suggestion box on 14 October, whether the class-cancellation resolution would be enforced on 18 November, and how the January term would change the schedule on 2 March 2004. Also named in the perfect attendance awards of 14 October 2003.

name: Lori Frey
seat: Congress member; vice chair, Legislative Research Committee
note: Named the new vice chair of Legislative Research on 16 September 2003 and approved in that post by Congress on 23 September 2003, when she also asked from the floor who had the final say on plus/minus grading.

name: Katie Jeter
seat: Congress member; vice chair, Public Relations Committee
note: Named the new vice chair of Public Relations on 16 September 2003 and approved by Congress on 23 September 2003. She was also named in the perfect attendance awards of 14 October 2003 and nominated Committee Member of September.

name: Katie Reynolds
seat: Congress member; secretary, Student Affairs Committee
note: Named the new secretary of the Student Affairs Committee on 16 September 2003, named in the perfect attendance awards of 14 October 2003, and nominated Committee Member of the Semester on 18 November 2003. A different person from Robert Reynolds.

name: Jessica Sutton
seat: Congress member; secretary, Public Relations Committee
note: Named the new secretary of the Public Relations Committee on 16 September 2003 and named in the perfect attendance awards of 14 October 2003. Not to be confused with Vice President of Administration Jessica Martin.

name: Melissa Constant
seat: Congress member
note: Spoke in the debate of 9 March 2004 against the January academic term, agreeing with John Law. She was also nominated Committee Member of the Month for January/February 2004 and thanked on 2 March 2004 for helping with a mailing during Congress.

name: Hollan Hohn
seat: Congress member; vice chair, Academic Affairs Committee; SGA representative to the University Senate
note: Read a personal statement against students paying for the Greek Village on 26 August 2003, questioned Dr. Kirchmeyer about directory access on 16 September, was appointed and then approved to the University Senate on 30 September and 7 October, was approved vice chair of Academic Affairs on 7 October, and questioned Robert Watkins during the constitution debate on 2 December. Surname printed both Hohn and Holm; see spelling doubts. Congress voted on 14 October 2003 to 'spell Hollan Hohn's name correctly'; the minutes also print the OCR variant 'Holm'.
